Millwall 0-1 Queens Park Rangers: Nicolas Madsen nets as QPR see off 10-man Lions
Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Millwall and Queens Park Rangers at the The Den on Saturday; Zak Sturge sees red early for Lions as Nicolas Madsen scores QPR winner.
Saturday 21 November 2026 14:34, UK
Nicolas Madsen's scruffy winner gave Queens Park Rangers their first away victory since August as they defeated Millwall 1-0 at The Den.
The result against their London rivals ensured the Hoops will end the weekend inside the play-off places in the Sky Bet Championship after they played the majority of the contest against 10 men following Zak Sturge's 15th-minute red card.
Despite a commendable defensive performance with depleted numbers, this was a third straight defeat for Millwall whose campaign continues to stutter.
Millwall began brightly, with their captain Jake Cooper nodding Camiel Neghli's cross into the path of Kyrell Lisbie - whose shot from an acute angle was saved by QPR goalkeeper Pierce Charles.
Ilias Chair tried to catch out Millwall's keeper, the returning Lukas Jensen, by trying his luck from just inside the Lions' half, with his audacious effort dipping wide.
Then came a big blow for the home side when Sturge was shown a straight red card for tripping Paul Smyth just outside the area as the last defender.
Smyth was then involved in an altercation on the touchline in the 24th minute that led to Millwall boss Alex Neil being shown a yellow card as the temperature in this London derby simmered.
Just when it looked as though the Lions would hold out until half-time, QPR took the lead in first-half stoppage time as Jensen first saved from Chair before Madsen's follow-up crossed the line despite Caleb Taylor's attempted heroics.
Millwall had goalkeeping coach Dean Thornton sent from the dugout in the aftermath and, short on numbers on the pitch, it looked a long way back for them in the second half.
The Hoops brought on Japanese midfielder Koki Saito at the break and he almost struck within six minutes of the restart when his shot from outside the box was pushed behind by Jensen.
Chair then curled a shot from the edge of the area narrowly wide and at this point it looked just a matter of time until the dominant visitors would score again.
But they were having a hard time of making all their possession count, with Richard Kone having a shot comfortably saved by Jensen as the match ticked towards the final 15 minutes.
QPR sub Karamoko Dembele had a good chance to make the game safe but his effort from Glen Kamara's cut-back went wide.
Jake Clarke-Salter was then narrowly off target from 25 yards in the 90th minute for the Hoops, for whom one goal proved to be enough.
